ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Samuel Johnson Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for severe recurrent depression and lifelong tics: depression work-up, sertraline and psychotherapy, safety assessment, and a request for neurology consultation. Concerns: He cannot work, cannot face his friends, and fears he is losing his mind; He has lived with movements and sounds he cannot fully control since childhood and wants to know what they are. [S]

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Sertraline started at 50 mg daily with a two-week tolerability check, and the dose adjusted by the PHQ-9
Weekly cognitive behavioral therapy for depression, with behavioral activation and work on self-reproach
PHQ-9 at every visit, structured safety assessment with a written safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, safety review at every visit, and a nurse phone check one week after starting
Neurology consultation to confirm the tic disorder, exclude other movement disorders, assess obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and advise on treatment
Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics (CBIT), eight sessions over ten weeks with a trained therapist, with psychoeducation for him and, if he wishes, his household
Tic severity measured with the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale at the consultation and at three and six months; tic medication held in reserve
PHQ-9 response (at least a 50% fall) by three months and remission (below 5) by six months
PHQ-9 10 at eleven weeks (from 21) and 4 at six months
Back at daily writing and seeing friends again by three months
Writing most mornings and dining with friends several times a week
Fewer and less disruptive tics, judged by him and by the tic severity scale, by six months
Yale Global Tic Severity Scale total tic score 22 from 30 and impairment 10 from 20; he finds the remaining tics manageable
Safety plan in place and reviewed at every visit
Reviewed at every visit; no suicidal thoughts at any visit

list.item: Independent in all activities; has written almost nothing for three months; avoids friends he usually sees daily; sight in one eye only [S]

Large man, untidily dressed; frequent tics during the interview: head turned toward the right shoulder and shaken, rocking, rubbing of the left knee, clucking and half-whistling sounds, blowing out his breath, and muttered phrases; speech slow but rich and precise; thought process logical; no delusions or hallucinations [S]

Mood "wretched"; affect constricted; guilt and self-reproach about idleness; fears he is losing his reason, which the examination does not support; PHQ-9 score 21 with item 9 scored 0; afraid of death; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-04-06: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with close follow-up because the depression is severe: weekly psychotherapy, a nurse phone check in one week, and a visit in two weeks. No current thoughts of suicide or self-harm, and no firearms or stockpiled medicines at home. A written safety plan was made with him and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline was given. Safety reviewed at every visit [S]
